Hallucinatory isolation establishes a boundary between internal and external reality, mathematically modeled as \( \mathcal{M} \rightarrow \mathcal{H} \) with \( \mathcal{H} \cap \mathcal{R} = \emptyset \). Imagination-as-affirmation links mental constructs directly to logical propositions, forming a kernel \( \text{Imag}(x) \rightarrow \text{Affirm}(x) \). Spinozan absorption introduces a temporal limit where \( \mathcal{M} \) converges to \( \mathcal{H} \), implying a fixed-point attractor in cognition. These operators form a closed system of belief propagation, where internal states dominate external reality, and attention becomes saturated with hallucinatory content. The failure mode occurs when \( \mathcal{M} \) cannot distinguish \( \mathcal{H} \) from \( \mathcal{R} \), resulting in epistemic collapse.
